profile.campus: Totowa, Passaic County, New Jersey (CyrusOne NYM2)
profile.reading:
Per CyrusOne's own facility page, NYM2 sits at 50 Madison Rd, Totowa, NJ 07512, a two-building, 200,000 sq ft campus (50,000 sq ft of data center space and 60,000 sq ft of work-area-recovery space) publishing 6 MW of IT capacity; CyrusOne describes the site as about 17 miles from Midtown Manhattan, integrated into its National IX connectivity platform.

Wikipedia's CyrusOne entry states the company acquired Cervalis, a Connecticut-area data center and colocation provider, in July 2015 for approximately $400 million, plausibly part of the same era of New York-metro expansion that added this New Jersey site, though CyrusOne's materials fetched this session did not directly confirm NYM2's acquisition origin; CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten and was taken private in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) acquired the company for approximately $15 billion.

Since going private under KKR and GIP ownership in 2022, CyrusOne has continued expanding its US and international footprint; the company's own press materials cite roughly $1 billion in cumulative capital investment in its San Antonio, Texas campuses alone as of a January 2025 groundbreaking, indicating continued growth investment across its portfolio under private ownership rather than a broad slowdown following the take-private transaction.

In November 2021, KKR and GIP first announced the agreement to acquire CyrusOne in an approximately $15 billion transaction, one of the largest data center M&A deals of that period, reflecting broader private-equity and infrastructure-fund interest in colocation real estate that has also driven acquisitions of peers like QTS (by Blackstone) and CoreSite (by American Tower) around the same era; CyrusOne's current published portfolio language describes more than 50 mission-critical facilities worldwide, though the company's own site and Wikipedia give somewhat different approximate totals (over 40 versus more than 50), neither of which this registry treats as a precise, independently verified figure.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Totowa publishes 6 MW of IT capacity across a two-building campus near Totowa, New Jersey, about 17 miles from Midtown Manhattan. The site comprises 50,000 square feet of data center space and 60,000 square feet of work area recovery space within 200,000 total square feet. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 6 MW of IT load is roughly 150 racks, though the operator's actual configuration is not published.

The campus holds SSAE 16 Type II certification, qualifying it for enterprises requiring audited security and availability controls. It ranks fourth by published capacity among five New Jersey facilities with disclosed megawatt figures, representing 5.4 percent of the state's 111.3 MW of published data center IT capacity. The state has 48 mapped facilities overall, most of which publish no capacity figures.

The site's proximity to Manhattan and integration into CyrusOne's National IX platform position it for New York metro enterprise and financial services tenants rather than large-scale AI training workloads. At 6 MW total, it is substantially smaller than the hyperscale campuses now driving US compute growth and grid constraint, and falls outside the scale at which individual facilities move national AI capacity trends.
